tasks.question: 保持 reproduce.c 的 fixed_depths={999,1000,1001} 和 require_null_terminated=1 不变，仅在编译 cJSON.c 时定义 CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT=1001。根据 parse_array/parse_object 在 depth 自增前执行的 >= 检查，预测三行 result、parse_end 和 input_len 中哪些字段会相对当前 result.txt 变化，并解释边界为什么移动一层。

point_checks.text: The comparison keeps fixed_depths={999,1000,1001}, require_null_terminated=1, the source revision, and the harness unchanged; the only treatment is defining CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT=1001 for the cJSON.c translation unit.
input_len remains 1999, 2001, and 2003 for depths 999, 1000, and 1001 respectively because the macro does not alter nested_array's 2*depth+1-byte JSON text.
The depth=999 and depth=1000 lines remain result=ok with parse_end equal to input_len (1999 and 2001 respectively).
The depth=1001 line changes from result=NULL parse_end=1000 input_len=2003 to result=ok parse_end=2003 input_len=2003.

The boundary moves by one level because parse_array and parse_object both test current depth >= limit before incrementing it; this array-only harness exercises parse_array, where limit 1001 admits entries at current depths 0 through 1000 and the old limit 1000 rejected the entry at current depth 1000.

forbidden_claim_checks.claim: With CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT=1001, depth 1001 still returns NULL at parse_end 1000.
Changing only CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT changes the three generated input lengths.
Either depth 999 or depth 1000 becomes a failure in the 1001-limit build.
The boundary shift is caused by changing the harness inputs or require_null_terminated.

tasks.reasoning: The fixed array generator is independent of the macro. The guards execute before depth increment. Fresh A/B compilation scoped to cJSON.c leaves lower cases/lengths unchanged and makes depth 1001 succeed at end 2003.

tasks.question: 现有观测中 depth=1000 成功，depth=1001 则 result=NULL 且 parse_end=1000。结合 nested_array 的构造、require_null_terminated=1、深度守卫与失败位置记录代码，哪些“末尾非 NUL”、“括号本身不配对”、“命中嵌套上限”或“普通分配失败”解释可由当前证据排除、支持或仍须额外实验？逐项给出证据边界。

point_checks.text: The current cases are balanced arrays generated as depth opening brackets, one zero, depth closing brackets, and a terminating NUL; the parser is called with require_null_terminated=1.
A missing terminal NUL is excluded for these generated inputs because nested_array writes the NUL and cJSON_ParseWithOpts includes it in buffer_length before enforcing require_null_terminated.
Mismatched brackets are excluded for these generated inputs because the generator emits equal counts of '[' and ']', and the depth=1000 instance of the same shape parses successfully.

Hitting the nesting limit is supported: the default is 1000, parse_array rejects when current depth is >= that limit before incrementing, and the observed transition is success at 1000 to failure at 1001 with failure offset 1000.

Ordinary internal allocation failure is neither established as the cause nor fully ruled out by the current run because cJSON has independent root/item allocation failure paths and the harness records no allocator event.

Distinguishing ordinary allocation failure requires an additional controlled experiment, such as allocator fault injection/telemetry or the limit-shift A/B while holding the input and build otherwise fixed.
parse_end=1000 is the recorded buffer.offset on failure and is consistent with the limit guard, but that offset alone is not a universal proof that every NULL result has the same cause.

forbidden_claim_checks.claim: The generated depth=1001 input lacks a terminating NUL.
The generated depth=1001 input has unbalanced brackets.
One successful reproduction definitively excludes every internal allocation failure.
parse_end=1000 proves that every possible NULL result is caused by CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT.
Ordinary allocation failure is established as the cause of the observed 1000/1001 boundary.

tasks.reasoning: The generator and NUL-including length wrapper exclude the proposed shape/NUL defects. The guard and boundary support the nesting explanation. Root/child allocation-failure paths and generic offset capture justify keeping allocation and universal-cause claims unproven.

tasks.question: 设计一个可立即执行的最小 A/B 验证：A 保持 run.sh 的默认编译，B 只为 cJSON.c 增加 -DCJSON_NESTING_LIMIT=1001，两者均运行同一 reproduce.c。写出具体编译/运行改动、预期区分两个假设的关键输出，以及哪种观测会否定“失败由固定嵌套上限触发”。

point_checks.text: A and B use the same checked source revision, compiler flags, include path, and reproduce.c; B's only semantic difference is CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT=1001 applied when cJSON.c is compiled.

From the repository root, an immediately executable A setup is:
  build_dir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/codeatlas-cjson-ab.XXXXXX")"
  cc -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -I corpus/cJSON -c examples/reproductions/cjson-nesting/reproduce.c -o "$build_dir/harness.o"
  cc -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -I corpus/cJSON -c corpus/cJSON/cJSON.c -o "$build_dir/cjson-a.o"
  cc "$build_dir/cjson-a.o" "$build_dir/harness.o" -lm -o "$build_dir/a"
  "$build_dir/a"

Reuse the same harness.o and build/run B with the define scoped to cJSON.c:
  cc -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -I corpus/cJSON -DCJSON_NESTING_LIMIT=1001 -c corpus/cJSON/cJSON.c -o "$build_dir/cjson-b.o"
  cc "$build_dir/cjson-b.o" "$build_dir/harness.o" -lm -o "$build_dir/b"
  "$build_dir/b"
Compare stdout directly; run.sh's diff still names the old A result and is not the B oracle.
A must print the current three lines: 999 ok/end 1999/len 1999; 1000 ok/end 2001/len 2001; 1001 NULL/end 1000/len 2003.
B should leave the 999 and 1000 lines unchanged and print depth=1001 result=ok parse_end=2003 input_len=2003.

A same-boundary B failure falsifies the nesting limit as a sufficient explanation only after confirming the macro override reached cJSON.c, holding the input and all other build factors fixed, and independently excluding a B-only allocation failure or another new failure through allocator telemetry and/or guard instrumentation; B failing by itself is inconclusive and requires diagnosis.

forbidden_claim_checks.claim: Change reproduce.c or its tested depths between A and B.
Apply the macro only to the harness while compiling cJSON.c separately without it.
Treat run.sh's expected diff against the old result.txt as the B result oracle.
Predict that B changes input_len for any tested depth.
Treat a B failure at the same boundary as direct falsification before independently excluding allocation failure or another newly introduced failure.

tasks.reasoning: The prescribed object-level A/B is executable and fresh outputs match. The revised falsifier now explicitly requires independently excluding B-only allocation or another new failure; B failure alone remains inconclusive. This is an approved conditional inference boundary, not a claim that allocator telemetry was executed here.

tasks.question: 保持当前 lwipopts.h 与调用顺序不变，只把 test_init 改成第一次返回 ERR_OK、第二次返回 ERR_IF。根据 netif_add 调用 init 和把 netif 插入 netif_list 的先后顺序，预测 add_second 以及 after_second 的 list/default 输出，并说明为什么第一个接口的状态不应被第二次初始化失败改写。

point_checks.text: Keep lwipopts.h and the call order unchanged, but make test_init return ERR_OK on its first invocation and ERR_IF on its second invocation.
add_first remains ok, while add_second prints failed because netif_add returns NULL when the second init call returns ERR_IF.
after_second prints list=first default=first.
netif_add calls init before it prepends the candidate to netif_list, so the failed second candidate never replaces first as the list head.

The already-linked first interface and the explicitly selected netif_default remain unchanged because the second failure returns before global list insertion and the harness does not call netif_set_default again; this does not imply every field written on the rejected second struct is rolled back.

forbidden_claim_checks.claim: The failed second interface is still inserted at the head of netif_list.
A failed second initialization changes netif_default to second or none.
The second failure removes or resets the already-linked first interface.
netif_add guarantees rollback of every field that init may have written on the rejected second struct.

tasks.reasoning: The init error returns before the global list insertion; the scoped failure probe preserves the first interface/default and prints add_second=failed. This does not promise rollback of every field on the rejected second struct.

tasks.question: 当前 result.txt 显示首次 netif_add 后 list=first 但 default=none，显式 netif_set_default(&first) 后 default=first，再添加 second 后 list=second 但 default=first。结合 which 的指针身份判定、链表头插代码和 netif_set_default，哪些“netif_add 会自动设默认”、“default 始终是链表头”、“第二次 add 未真正入链”解释可被逐一排除？说明每个结论依赖的观测。

point_checks.text: The printed names are pointer-identity observations: which maps NULL to none, &first to first, and &second to second.
The hypothesis that netif_add automatically sets the default is excluded by add_first=ok followed by after_first list=first default=none.
The hypothesis that default is always an alias of the list head is excluded by after_second list=second default=first after first was explicitly made default.
The hypothesis that the second add did not link second is excluded by add_second=ok and the immediate pointer-identity observation list=second.
The mechanism matches the observations: successful netif_add prepends only netif_list, while netif_set_default assigns netif_default separately.

forbidden_claim_checks.claim: netif_add automatically made first the default despite after_first default=none.
netif_default must always equal netif_list.
The successful second add was not linked even though which(netif_list) returned second.
The labels first and second are inferred from interface names rather than pointer identity.

tasks.reasoning: which compares addresses; the rerun demonstrates both successful linking and divergence of list/default. The source has separate list and default assignments, supporting all three exclusions.

tasks.question: 为验证 netif_default 与 netif_list 是可独立改变的状态，在现有 harness 的 after_second 打印后插入 netif_set_default(NULL)，并立即用 which 再打印 list/default，其他操作不变。写出最小代码改动、预期新输出，以及若 list 也随之变为 none 将否定源码机制中的什么判断。

point_checks.text: Insert the probe immediately after the existing after_second print and before either netif_remove call, with all earlier operations unchanged.
The minimal change is netif_set_default(NULL) followed by a printf that passes netif_list and netif_default through which, for example after_clear_default list=%s default=%s.
The new line should be after_clear_default list=second default=none.
netif_set_default(NULL) assigns NULL only to netif_default (aside from route bookkeeping) and contains no write to netif_list, whose declaration is a separate global.

If this isolated call also made the printed list become none, it would falsify the source-based mechanism claim that clearing the default leaves netif_list unchanged and that the two observed pointer states can be varied independently; it would require investigating an unaccounted side effect, build/configuration mismatch, or other operation.

forbidden_claim_checks.claim: The expected post-clear list is none.
The expected post-clear default remains first.
netif_set_default(NULL) removes second or first from netif_list.
A list=none observation would confirm that list and default are independent.

tasks.reasoning: The insertion point precedes removals, and the clear-default probe changes only default to none while list stays second. An isolated contrary observation would invalidate that mechanism prediction and require investigation rather than confirm independence.
